events.system:
P = 4-[4-(hydroxymethyl)phenyl]butan-2-one
P --[(i) Na; (ii) CH₃I]--> Q
Q --[Ph₃P=CH₂]--> R
R --[mCPBA]--> S
S --[CH₃NH₂]--> T
R --[(i) Hg(OAc)₂, CH₃OH; (ii) NaBH₄]--> U
Q --[CH₃OH (excess), dry HCl]--> V
events.hidden_link: P undergoes selective Williamson ether synthesis at the primary alcohol to give Q, preserving the methyl ketone. Q is converted to alkene R via Wittig olefination. R undergoes epoxidation to S, which is opened by methylamine at the less hindered terminal carbon to give tertiary alcohol T. Alkoxymercuration of R yields the Markovnikov ether U, which lacks a stereocentre due to two identical methyl groups. Q forms ketal V with excess methanol.
events.route: 1. P -> Q: Na deprotonates the primary alcohol (ketones do not react to form stable enolates under these conditions that outcompete alkoxide formation for methylation), and CH3I forms the methyl ether. 2. Q -> R: Wittig reaction changes C=O to C=CH2. 3. R -> S: mCPBA forms an epoxide at the alkene. 4. S -> T: CH3NH2 acts as a nucleophile, attacking the less hindered carbon of the epoxide in an SN2 fashion, yielding a tertiary alcohol. 5. R -> U: Alkoxymercuration-demercuration with CH3OH adds -OCH3 to the more substituted carbon of the double bond (Markovnikov addition), giving a tertiary ether with two identical methyl groups, hence achiral. 6. Q -> V: Excess methanol and dry HCl convert the ketone into a dimethyl ketal.
events.student_must_notice: The regioselectivity of epoxide opening under basic/neutral conditions (attack at less hindered carbon) yielding a tertiary alcohol (positive Lucas test), and the Markovnikov alkoxymercuration yielding an achiral product.
events.trap: Students might incorrectly predict the epoxide opening at the more substituted carbon (acidic conditions), yielding a primary alcohol (no immediate Lucas test). They might also assume Markovnikov addition creates a stereocentre in U, failing to notice the two identical methyl groups.
events.given: The reaction scheme starting from P.
events.asked: Properties of compounds Q, T, U, and V.
events.why_hard: Requires precise tracking of functional groups and regioselectivity across multiple parallel branches, with specific traps involving stereocentre counting and Lucas test reactivity.

members.working: P = p-(HOCH2)C6H4CH2CH2COCH3. (i) Na, (ii) CH3I converts the benzylic OH to OCH3, giving Q = p-(CH3OCH2)C6H4CH2CH2COCH3. Q is a methyl ketone, so it gives a positive iodoform test (D true). Q + Ph3P=CH2 (Wittig) replaces the C=O with =CH2: R = CH2=C(CH3)CH2CH2-C6H4-CH2OCH3. R + mCPBA gives the epoxide S; ring opening with CH3NH2 attacks the less substituted carbon, giving T = (CH3)(ArCH2CH2)(CH2NHCH3)C-OH, a tertiary alcohol — immediate turbidity with Lucas reagent (A true). R + Hg(OAc)2/MeOH then NaBH4 gives Markovnikov methoxylation: U = CH3-C(OCH3)(CH3)-CH2CH2-Ar-CH2OCH3; the methoxy-bearing carbon has two identical CH3 groups, so U has 0 stereocentres (B true) and only 1 stereoisomer, not 2 (C false). Correct options: ABD.
